newsitem.title: CANADA: Martin says pressure on Canada to keep rates down.
newsitem.headline: Martin says pressure on Canada to keep rates down.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin on Thursday shrugged aside pressure from some of his Liberal colleagues to spend more money in Prime Minister Jean Chretien's second term.
"The pressure on us is in fact to stay the course and make sure that interest rates stay down and jobs are created," Martin told reporters after a cabinet strategy session.
Martin did indicate, however, that the Canadian government might spend more money if the government betters its deficit targets.

Asked if there would be any new spending before the deficit is eliminated, Martin said, "I think if you take a look at it in fact what we did in our last budget as an example of when we are substantially ahead of our track, we did (spend)."

We put C$800 million into the Canadian Foundation for Innovation, we put C$850 million into the Canadian Child Tax Benefit, and so we have indicated that we are going to deal with the nation's priorities, and we will do so at the same time as eliminating the deficit, and we will maintain the course."
Asked when the government would spend more to attack child poverty, he said, "When the money is available, when the nation's finances permit it, then we will be able to move."

"If you take a look at the last budget, if you take a look at the party platform (for the June 2 election), we've indicated very clearly that we are going to be staying the course and we always indicated what our priorties are," Martin said.
